projection.title: Projection and what-ifs
projection.subtitle: How long the assets you could sell from last, year by year.
projection.countedOnOverview: Which income and outgoing lines count is set on the
projection.baselineHint: Assets outlast outgoings for this long
projection.chartAssets: Assets you could sell from, over time
projection.incomeIndexed: Income rises with inflation too (rents, indexed pensions)
projection.inflationHint: Tick the lines that rise with inflation. Untick amounts that stay the same, like a fixed mortgage payment or a fixed rent. Saved with the plan.
projection.inflationTotals: Rising with inflation: {{rising}} a month · Staying the same: {{fixed}} a month
projection.incomeNotIndexed: Income does not rise with inflation (the box above is off).
projection.spendFromHint: Any year income falls short of outgoings, the shortfall is covered by selling the ticked assets in proportion to their value. Property and vehicles are left out by default. The percentage is each asset's own growth a year: its growth rule where it has one, otherwise 0. Type a rate to change it here.
projection.tempHint: Exists only in this plan and is saved with it. It is not added to your assets. Leave the year at 0 for something you have now, or set the year the money arrives. The type matters only in the Simulate tab: stocks swing and fall in a crash, bonds less, property in between, and cash or fixed do not move.
projection.hoverHint: Hover a year for each asset's value, income, outgoings and what was sold.
projection.leftAtEndHint: Assets you sell from, at the end of the drawdown
projection.strategyOrdered: In my order (set it per asset below)
projection.drawdownNote: Before the start year surpluses are saved and shortfalls are assumed to be paid from earnings that are not modelled.
projection.sellOrder: Sell order (1 sells first, blank sells last)
projection.describeSpend: {{amount}} a month from {{from}}, instead of the recurring outgoings
projection.label: Name
projection.yearsHint: Years count from this year: 0 = now, 3 = three years from now.
projection.disclaimer: A planning aid, not a forecast. No taxes and no loan repayments. The ticks above and on the lists below decide what is counted.
projection.taxesHint: Used for any line without a rate of its own. Income is your recurring credits (salary, pension) and income what-ifs; yields are what an asset pays out as a share of its value; rent is the fixed amount an asset brings in. Gains are taxed when you sell, and a sale is sized so that what arrives after tax covers the cost.
projection.bufferHint: A buffer holds that many years of costs in cash from the first drawdown year. It is spent first, and refilled only after a year in which your other assets did not fall, so a crash is sat out on cash. It matters most in the Simulate tab.
projection.countsUntil: {{name}} counts until the end of this year
projection.countsUntilHint: Last year this line counts, such as the year a mortgage is paid off. Empty means it never stops.
projection.taxMoved: Tax rates are set per line on the Tax tab.
projection.livingHint: Spending on top of your recurring costs, such as day-to-day living and travel. Change it and watch what happens to the runway.
projection.livingInflates: Living and travel rises with inflation
projection.livingStepsHint: Each box shows the runway, and the assets left at the end of the plan, if living and travel were that much. Click one to use it.

retirement.skipped: {{count}} item(s) in another currency without a conversion are not counted

simulate.successHint: Assets you would sell from last all {{years}} years
simulate.typicalEndHint: Assets left at the end, the middle future

simulate.runsOutHint: The middle year among futures that run dry

simulate.depletedTitle: Share of futures that have run out by each year
simulate.sweepSubtitle: Chance the money lasts, for different spending levels (columns, against your planned costs) and how often crashes happen (rows).
simulate.cellTitle: Spending at {{spend}}% of plan, crash chance {{crash}}% a year
simulate.resilient: At a {{crash}}% yearly crash chance, spending up to {{spend}}% of the plan still lasts 9 times in 10.
simulate.resilientNone: At a {{crash}}% yearly crash chance, even 80% of the planned spending lasts less than 9 times in 10.
simulate.sweepHint: Each cell is {{runs}} futures, so neighbouring cells vary a little.
simulate.crashChanceHint: Chance of a crash in any one year.
simulate.slumpYearsHint: Years of weaker growth following a crash.
simulate.slumpCutHint: Share of the expected growth that goes missing.
simulate.inflationSpreadHint: How far inflation drifts from your plan's rate.
simulate.classesHint: Its growth rate in the plan is its long-run average. The type decides how wildly it swings and how much of a crash it takes. Fixed means no swings.
simulate.disclaimer: A stress test, not a forecast. Crashes hit stocks fully, property partly and bonds a little; cash and fixed assets are not hit. Taxes apply as set on the Tax tab.
simulate.fanHintToday: Amounts are in today's money: each future's own inflation is taken out. The dark band holds half of the futures, the light band eight in ten.
simulate.bufferTitle: What is a cash buffer worth?
simulate.bufferSubtitle: The same futures with different buffers: years of costs kept in cash, spent first and refilled only after a year in which your other assets did not fall.
simulate.bufferHint: Each column is {{runs}} futures. A buffer costs growth in good years and pays off in bad ones, so the right size depends on the crash settings below. Taxes and your selling order apply.
simulate.rateIncludesCrashesHint: Treats each asset's growth in the plan as its long-run average, crashes included (as historical averages are), so the typical future matches the projection and crashes show up as risk around it. Untick to add crashes on top of the rate, which is much harsher.

fullReport.hoverHint: Hover a year on any chart for the numbers behind it.
fullReport.soldHint: Gross amounts sold each year to cover the shortfall (costs and tax, less income), by asset. Tax withheld on gains is taken out of what is sold. The last column is what is left to sell from.
fullReport.runsDry: The assets you sell from run out in {{year}}; costs after that are not covered.
fullReport.nothingSold: No assets are sold in this plan over {{years}} years: income covers the costs.

fullReport.simulationMissing: The stress test was not included.

tax.totalHint: All kinds, in the money of each year
tax.share: Tax as a share of money in
tax.shareHint: Of all income, yields, rent and sales received
tax.today: Tax on income today, a year
tax.todayHint: Of {{gross}} before tax: income, yields and rent
tax.secIncomeHint: Recurring credits the plan counts, such as a salary or a pension.
tax.secWhatIfHint: Extra income you added as a what-if.
tax.secYieldHint: What assets pay out as a share of their value: dividends, interest, coupons.
tax.secRentHint: Fixed income from assets, such as a rental.
tax.secGainsHint: Tax on the gain, the value above what an asset cost, when you sell from it. Only the gain is taxed, and a sale is sized so what arrives after tax covers the cost.

field.name: Name
field.outcome: What it does when it matches
field.outcomeHint: Link binds the payment on its own. Suggest sends it to the queue below for you to confirm.
field.window: How far apart the dates may be
field.windowHint: Late is counted from the due date, early from the day the invoice was written, so paying the day after issue is not weeks early.
field.similarityHint: From 0 to 1. Leave empty to ignore the description entirely.
field.scopeHint: Leave empty to apply to everything
field.foreignOnly: Only currencies other than the one this workspace uses
field.textHint: Several, separated by commas, means any of them.
field.triggerHint: Matching happens at two moments, and the evidence is not the same in both.
field.amountMatch: How close the amount must be
field.amountMatchHint: Compared against what is still owed, not the original total.
field.amountBandHint: About the payment itself: a size you do or do not want this rule handling.
field.transferSignalsHint: The two legs are always on different accounts. These say what else has to be true before the pair is trusted.
field.accountTypes: Only when one side is one of these
field.amountMatchHintTransfer: Compared against the other leg, in the same currency. Different currencies never pair on their own; you can still link the two legs by hand.
field.windowHintTransfer: Money rarely lands on the day it left. Both sides are counted from the other record, so two days either way covers a weekend.

amount.ratioHint: Uses the withholding rates for your country. Nothing matches until those are set.
amount.partialHint: For payments made in instalments. What is left stays open, and the next payment matches it exactly.
amount.setHint: For a payment that covers more than one invoice. If more than one combination adds up, we ask instead of choosing.
amount.setFeeHint: A share of what the invoices are worth, for a payment that moves net of a cut. Zero means the total must be exact.

queue.title: Waiting for you
queue.empty: Nothing to review. Everything matched on its own.
queue.declineHint: Not a match. This pair will not be suggested again.
queue.declined: Dismissed. We will not ask again
queue.mayPairWith: may be the other half of {{name}}

step.whichHint: Leave everything empty and it looks at all of it
step.match: When it counts as a match
step.matchHint: How closely the payment and the promise have to fit
step.matchHintTransfer: How close the two records have to be

trigger.money_arrives: When money comes in or goes out
trigger.money_arrivesHint: The payment shows up on the statement and we look for the invoice it settles.
trigger.invoice_issuedHint: The payment came first and the invoice follows, so we look back at money already there.
trigger.bothHint: The rule is trusted either way round.
